# Lintel v4.0 — The Reframe (master design doc)

**Generated by:** `/office-hours` on 2026-05-29
**Status:** DRAFT_FOR_REVIEW — 5 chapters · 1 architecture · awaiting operator pass
**Mode:** Builder (engineering scaffolding for the next generation of Lintel)
**Supersedes:** none — extends v3.5 doc-gen, v3.6 cohort backlog, v3.7 frontend family, v3.8 jobs + planner-module

> Five things landed on the desk in one session: two design docs, one text request about engineering depth, and a meta-process note about infrastructure-for-infrastructure. They're not five separate features. They are **one coherent reframe** — what Lintel **is**, what every workflow inside it **must guarantee**, how depth gets specced for the engineering domains we actually live in, and how Lintel evolves itself without breaking what already runs.

---

## Status, scope, and how to read this

This is the master design doc for v4.0. It consolidates:

1. **[lintel-feature-spine-packs-navigation.md](../../docs/feature-requests/lintel-feature-spine-packs-navigation.md)** — generic spine extraction, pack architecture, navigation as requirement, CAIP-SE as reference pack (FR-A through FR-D)
2. **[lintel-feature-brief-forge.md](../../docs/feature-requests/lintel-feature-brief-forge.md)** — universal hand-off gate, standardized envelope, generated 1:1 wiki (FR-A through FR-C)
3. **Text-form request — engineering-depth** — exceptional quality across Technical Architecture, Data Architecture, Security & Compliance, DevOps & Hosting, Testing & QA
4. **Text-form meta-process** — process for "building infrastructure for infrastructure"
5. **Operator stance carried through** — bold, effective, operator carries responsibility; opinionated harness; refuses padding for novice protection

The doc is structured as five chapters that build on each other. They are **shippable independently** but **most valuable together**. Where I interpret rather than mirror the operator's spec, I flag it explicitly. Where I disagree, I say so before proposing.

---

## The insight: these are one architecture, not five features

Spend ten minutes mapping how the four operator-provided inputs depend on each other and the picture clicks into place:

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  LINTEL v4.0 CORE                                                         │
│                                                                           │
│  Chapter 1 → SPINE    (generic engine, neutral on content)               │
│  Chapter 1 → PACK     (identity loaded in at session-start)              │
│  Chapter 1 → NAV      (entry/exit declarations + orientator at SENSE)    │
│  Chapter 2 → FORGE    (universal hand-off gate at every boundary)        │
│  Chapter 2 → ENVELOPE (standardized payload — head/body/tail)            │
│  Chapter 2 → WIKI     (generated from sources of truth, 1:1)             │
│  Chapter 3 → DEPTH    (5 engineering domain modules)                     │
│  Chapter 4 → META     (infrastructure-for-infrastructure discipline)     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

How they compose:

   Operator types something
        ↓
   SPINE reads PACK (identity, defaults, policies)
        ↓
   NAVIGATION'S orientator agent reads request + pack + open jobs
        ↓
   → picks workflow + entry-phase + risk-level
        ↓
   workflow_root spawns job (v3.8 jobs system)
        ↓
   At each phase transition → FORGE evaluates → produces ENVELOPE
        ↓
   Within BUILD, ENGINEERING DOMAIN MODULES may activate
        ↓
   Each domain has its own gates, loops, recovery, checkpoints
        ↓
   META-INFRA mode applies if work is harness-on-harness
        ↓
   CAPTURE writes envelopes + lessons + ADRs
        ↓
   WIKI regenerates from all of it
```

**The reframe is not "Lintel grows new features." It's "Lintel becomes what its own architecture has been pointing toward since v3.6."** Every previous milestone — the cohort sequencing, the frontend family separation, the jobs system, the planner-as-module — was a step toward this. v4.0 is the consolidation, not an invention.

---

## Architecture before details — warming up

Before walking the chapters, the three load-bearing observations from re-reading the v3.5 → v3.8 work:

**A — Lintel already does most of this informally.** BUILD scene-sets implementer subagents with task text + criteria + companion skills (`skills/build/SKILL.md:66-72`). Cycle propagates state between phases. Hooks fire at the right moments. Lessons compound. **v4.0 makes the informal mechanical.** The risk of a re-write disguised as a refactor is real; the antidote is the meta-infra discipline in Chapter 4.

**B — The L-trio + L-004 already shape what this reframe must respect.**
- L-001 (scaffolding-not-content): packs ship as content; the spine ships as scaffolding. The whole reframe is L-001 made architectural.
- L-002 (grep-first): the FR-A spine extraction audit IS L-002 applied at the level of "what's hardcoded that shouldn't be."
- L-003 (verify counts): every claim in this doc (which skill references Trailblazer, which hooks are MS-specific, how many CLIs have manifests) needs verification before code.
- L-004 (separate decisions from execution): spine = execution-engine; packs = decision-layer. The clearest L-004 application yet.

**C — Operator's bold-and-responsible stance is the design constraint, not a style.** Every gate ships with `--override` + audit. Every novice protection that would slow the operator is refused. Pack policies are configured once and apply mechanically. The system trusts the operator to use the override responsibly.

# CHAPTER 1 — Generic spine + packs + navigation

> Honors `lintel-feature-spine-packs-navigation.md` end-to-end. Adds my interpretation and one decision-recommendation per FR.

## 1.1 Why this chapter goes first

Without spine extraction (FR-A), every other chapter depends on something contaminated by CAIP-SE assumptions. Without packs (FR-B), the spine has nothing to read at session-start. Without navigation (FR-C), workflow_root declarations are advisory. Without CAIP-SE lifted into pack format (FR-D), operator's own daily workflow breaks during the transition.

**Ship order: A → B → D → C** (D before C lets orientator test against a real pack).

## 1.2 FR-A — Spine extraction (verbatim agreement + 2 adds)

Operator's spec stands. Add two items:

**A.7 — Pack-resolver test harness.** Per L-002, the resolver becomes a critical-path interface used by ~30+ skills. Ship `tests/unit/pack-resolver-fallbacks.sh` BEFORE A.3 (replace hardcoded references). Test: with no pack active, every resolver call returns the neutral default; with a mock pack active, returns pack values. Without this test, A.3 risks silent regression where a swap leaves a hardcoded reference behind.

**A.8 — Audit deliverable as PR artifact.** A.1 ("audit core skills for pack-specific assumptions") produces a list. That list should ship as `docs/v4.0/spine-extraction-audit.md` in the FR-A PR. Future readers (and future re-extractions for new pack-bound concepts) need the inventory.

## 1.3 FR-B — Pack architecture (verbatim agreement + decisions)

Pack schema, lifecycle skills, inheritance, validation hook — all sound. Three open decisions in operator's note. **My recommendations:**

| Decision | Operator option | Recommendation | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ms-internal` base pack | "now or later?" | **NOW** | Costs ~1h. Pays dividends the moment any sister-pack to CAIP-SE shows up. Defer = certain regret + force-rewrite of CAIP-SE later. |
| Pack-versioning enforcement | "warn-only or block-on-incompatible?" | **warn-only for v4.0; block from v4.1** | Pack ecosystem doesn't exist yet. Block-on-incompat in v4.0 is theater. Warn lets the discipline form before it bites. |
| Default `auto_mode_eligible` | "true or false by convention?" | **false** | Conservative for a new mechanism. Operator opts in per workflow once they've watched the orientator behave on their patterns. |

**One add I want: `pack.yaml` includes a `brief_forge:` block** (per Chapter 2). The FR-B spec doesn't include it because Brief Forge was in a separate doc; v4.0 unifies them. The pack manifest must include `brief_forge:` policy at v4.0 ship-time, not retrofit later.

## 1.4 FR-C — Navigation (verbatim agreement + tweak)

Mandatory `navigation:` block on every `workflow_root: true` skill: agreed. Orientator agent at SENSE: agreed. Auto-mode level (b) — auto-start low-risk, confirm high-risk: agreed and matches the operator's stance everywhere else.

**Tweak: orientator escalation budget is pack-configurable.**

Operator's spec says "Hard budget: orientator's total LLM usage ≤ 2k tokens per SENSE." Hard-coding 2k means the budget can't be tuned per pack. A pack that lives in low-friction terrain (internal tooling, hotfix work) might want 500 tokens. A pack handling complex customer-engagement intent might want 5k.

**Proposal:** `pack.yaml` declares:

```yaml
navigation:
  orientator_budget_tokens: 2000   # default 2k, pack-overridable
  escalation_threshold: medium     # never|low|medium|high — when to invoke LLM at all
```

Mechanical-first stays. The escalation budget becomes a policy, not a constant.

## 1.5 FR-D — CAIP-SE as reference pack (verbatim agreement + sequencing note)

The migration is mechanical (`git mv`-heavy). The decision flag in the operator's note is the `ms-internal` base pack — covered above (recommend now).

**Sequencing note:** FR-D ships BEFORE FR-C. Reason: orientator-agent needs a real, non-trivial pack to test against. Default `_default` pack is too thin to exercise the routing logic. Doing D before C means orientator's first integration tests use a substantive pack, surfacing real edge cases instead of synthetic ones.

## 1.6 What v4.0 changes about today's mental model

| Today's concept | After Chapter 1 |
|---|---|
| Lintel = MS-CAIP-SE harness | Lintel = harness with CAIP-SE as one pack |
| WorkProfile = system concept | WorkProfile = `compliance.workprofile_default` in pack |
| Trailblazer voice = always relevant | Trailblazer voice = active when `caip-se` pack loaded |
| `personas.md` template = sales engineer | `personas.md` template = whatever active pack defines |
| `/li:cycle` always assumes compliance | `/li:cycle` reads pack at SENSE; compliance fires per pack policy |

**This is a contract change for any operator currently using Lintel for CAIP-SE work.** Migration is `/li:pack-switch caip-se` after FR-D ships. After that, behavior is identical to today.

## 1.7 Chapter 1 risks

- **Risk: spine extraction misses a hardcoded reference.** Mitigation: pack-resolver test harness (A.7) + post-merge `grep -r` audit shipped as second PR artifact.
- **Risk: pack inheritance creates surprise.** Mitigation: `extends:` is shallow-merged with explicit precedence, documented in `docs/concepts/pack-inheritance.md`, regression tests on every example.
- **Risk: orientator gets the route wrong on ambiguous requests.** Mitigation: auto-mode level (b) confirms on high-risk; `auto_mode_eligible: false` default; `--no-auto` always works.

# CHAPTER 2 — Brief Forge + envelope + generated wiki

> Honors `lintel-feature-brief-forge.md` end-to-end. Three adds, one renaming proposal, one composition note.

## 2.1 The architectural purpose of this chapter

Chapter 1 gives the spine an identity and a router. Chapter 2 gives it **a contract at every boundary crossing**. Without Brief Forge, the new spine+packs system can still pass uncurated payloads between phases — meaning all the work in Chapter 1 produces a flexible engine that still has the same hand-off-quality drift as today's Lintel.

Brief Forge isn't a feature on top of v3.8. **It's the layer that finally lets v4.0's mechanical engine produce mechanical quality.**

## 2.2 FR-A — Brief Forge (verbatim agreement + 3 adds)

The three-phase mechanic (curate → hydrate → dispatch), pack-driven policy, parallel evaluators, single budget, override-with-audit — all sound. Three adds:

**A.1 — Evaluator registry as separate concept.** Operator's spec lists 7 evaluators (security/compliance/voice/stale/completeness/knowledge-overlap/legality). Packs need to declare CUSTOM evaluators too — e.g., a customer-engagement pack might want a `kost-attestation-eval` that checks customer-budget claims. Ship a registry:

```
lib/brief-forge/evaluators/
├── _registry.yaml          # built-in evaluator declarations
├── security-eval.sh
├── compliance-eval.sh
├── ...
```

Pack manifests reference by name. Custom evaluators live in `packs/<pack>/brief-forge/evaluators/` and the registry auto-discovers them.

**A.2 — Per-handoff-type policy granularity.** Operator's spec has `evaluators.on_subagent_spawn: [...]` etc. Good. Add explicit per-handoff-type opt-in `enabled: true|false` so a pack can disable forge for a handoff-type entirely without removing all evaluators:

```yaml
brief_forge:
  on_subagent_spawn:
    enabled: true
    evaluators: [security-eval]
  on_phase_transition:
    enabled: false   # pack-decision: phase-transitions don't need forge in this pack
```

Default is `enabled: true` if `evaluators:` is non-empty.

**A.3 — Renaming consideration: keep "Brief Forge" or call it "Hand-off Gate"?** "Brief Forge" is evocative but the name suggests document-creation. The thing actually does gate-evaluation. **Recommendation: keep "Brief Forge"** because (a) operator already locked it in, (b) the forging metaphor fits the curate-hydrate-dispatch flow, (c) renaming for taste isn't worth the doc-churn. Logging this as considered-and-declined.

## 2.3 FR-B — Envelope (verbatim agreement + schema home)

Standardized payload envelope with HEAD + BODY + TAIL: agreed. Adoption mandatory at workflow_root: agreed.

**Schema home:** Operator's spec doesn't pin where the envelope schema lives. **Proposal:** `lib/envelope-schema.yaml` (single source of truth, JSON-schema-style validation). Tests reference it. Documentation generates from it. Future schema-version bumps go through the meta-infra mode (Chapter 4).

**Envelope-replay UX:** Operator wants `li-envelope-replay <envelope-id>`. **One detail:** replay should default to **dry-run** (re-execute in sandbox, surface what would happen). Actual re-execution requires `--apply` flag. Reason: envelopes capture state at the moment of hand-off; the world may have moved on. Dry-run + diff against now lets the operator decide.

## 2.4 FR-C — Generated 1:1 wiki (verbatim agreement + composition)

Wiki generator script reading frontmatter + manifests + navigation + envelope schema: agreed. Initial wiki structure: agreed.

**Composition with the showcase.** The current showcase (`docs/showcase/lintel-the-harness.html`) is hand-curated v3.8. **Proposal:** the same `bin/li-wiki-gen` regenerates the showcase from current sources. Two outputs from one generator: the markdown wiki (developer-facing reference) and the showcase HTML (operator-facing system map). Both reflect ground truth. Both regenerate on the same trigger.

This solves the gap noted in the v3.7 showcase: "wiki vs showcase drift" was already a risk. v4.0 closes it.

**CI enforcement:** Operator's spec asks "fail build, or warn-only?" **Recommendation: warn-only for v4.0; fail from v4.1.** Same logic as pack-version block-vs-warn — let the discipline form before it bites.

## 2.5 Chapter 2 risks

- **Risk: Brief Forge adds perceptible latency.** Mitigation: 5k-token budget total, mechanical-first, evaluators run in parallel where possible. Telemetry from day one to verify <1s overhead claim.
- **Risk: envelope schema becomes a god-object.** Mitigation: required fields are minimal (HEAD has 6, TAIL has 4); BODY is free-form per `content_type`. Schema versioning from v1 means breaking changes are visible.
- **Risk: wiki generation forks reality.** Mitigation: generator runs as pre-commit hook + CI check; manual edits to wiki are flagged as "to be regenerated" by the staleness-check.

# CHAPTER 3 — Engineering domain depth

> This chapter is my interpretation of the operator's text-form request. The request asked for exceptional quality across five engineering domains, with granularity from full-process to single-action, with checkpoints, recovery, iteration, and modular flexibility. Operator said this is "VERY important." Honoring that by giving it the deepest specification of any chapter.

## 3.1 What the operator asked for, in my words

The text request, parsed:

- **Five domains** must be exceptional: Technical Architecture, Data Architecture, Security & Compliance, DevOps & Hosting, Testing & QA.
- Each domain needs **granularity** — from "do the full process" to "do this single action."
- **Preferences** live in main profile.
- **Process for engineering matters more than current depth** — there should be enough hops, gradual context production, checkpoints, failure recovery, continuation-after-fix without breaking, raise-help when needed.
- **Each section has its own quality loop** — things must qualify to move on.
- **Flexible / comprehensive / capable / iterable / modular / opinionated** are the qualities to replicate across the whole action-system.
- "We are not the dumb tool" — Lintel integrates from a very technical perspective; operator chooses entry granularity.

**My interpretation:** Lintel today has these five domains scattered across skills, agents, and hooks but no domain-level **modules** that compose into a full engineering workflow. The reframe makes each domain a first-class composable unit.

## 3.2 The Engineering Domain Module pattern

Each of the five domains becomes a **module**: a workflow_root skill with its own sub-skills, agents, hooks, gates, and loops. Modules can be invoked standalone, called from inside BUILD as a sub-module, OR composed into a "full engineering pass."

```yaml
# Pattern: every engineering domain module declares this shape
name: <domain>-module
layer: foundation
workflow_root: true                    # spawns its own job
description: <domain> as a callable module — full / loop / single-action granularity

navigation:                            # per Chapter 1
  valid_entries: [full, loop, single]
  valid_exits: [<gate-name>]
  auto_mode_eligible: false
  risk_level: medium

brief_forge:                           # per Chapter 2
  on_subagent_spawn:
    enabled: true
    evaluators: [<domain>-eval, security-eval]
  on_phase_transition:
    enabled: true
    evaluators: [completeness-eval]

domain:                                # NEW concept for v4.0
  preferences_root: engineering.<domain>.*  # in main profile
  granularities:
    - full                             # full domain pass — multi-phase loop
    - loop                             # one iteration loop in the domain
    - single                           # one action (e.g., "review API contract")
  checkpoints:
    - <name>: <pass-criterion>
  recovery:
    - on_failure: <strategy>
  continuation:
    - after_fix: <how-to-resume>
  raise_help:
    - <when>: <to-whom>
```

Each module ships with:

- Its own `SKILL.md` + sub-skill family
- A dedicated agent set (most reused from existing 83 agents, augmented as needed)
- 2-5 hooks specific to its concerns
- A scoring rubric (similar to frontend-design-review's 6-dim audit)
- A failure-recovery playbook
- An iteration loop spec

## 3.3 Module spec — `tech-architecture` (TA)

**Purpose:** When the work has architectural depth (new service, API design, dependency restructure, cross-system boundary), invoke TA to produce architecture-grade decisions and contracts.

**Granularities:**

| Entry | When | Outputs |
|---|---|---|
| `/li:ta full` | new project / major scope change | system-arch.md + ADR set + interface contracts + dependency graph + non-functional reqs |
| `/li:ta loop` | mid-cycle architecture iteration | revised ADRs + diff against prior decisions + impact analysis |
| `/li:ta single --action <name>` | targeted operation | one of: api-design / dependency-audit / complexity-budget / boundary-review / scaling-plan |

**Sub-skills (proposed):**

- `ta-api-design` — REST/GraphQL/gRPC interface design with versioning + breaking-change analysis
- `ta-dependency-graph` — module dependency map, circular-detection, layering audit
- `ta-complexity-audit` — per-component cyclomatic + cognitive complexity scoring
- `ta-boundary-review` — bounded-context drift detection, leaking-abstraction flags
- `ta-scaling-plan` — capacity model + bottleneck identification + cost-projection
- `ta-contract-collision` — change-impact analysis across consumers of an interface
- `ta-quality-attributes` — non-functional requirement spec (performance, reliability, observability)

**Agents (mostly existing):**

- `agents/engineering/Architect.md` (existing — primary)
- `agents/engineering/BackendArchitect.md` (existing)
- `agents/engineering/APIDesigner.md` (existing)
- `agents/engineering/SystemArchitect.md` (NEW — system-of-systems thinking)
- `agents/engineering/CapacityPlanner.md` (NEW — scaling model)

**Hooks:**

- `arch-drift-warn` (NEW) — pre-edit on files claimed by an ADR's "decisions" block: warns if change contradicts the ADR
- `contract-collision-warn` (NEW) — pre-edit on an interface file with declared consumers: warns
- `complexity-budget-warn` (NEW) — pre-commit if cyclomatic exceeds threshold from preferences

**Checkpoints (within loop):**

1. **Discovery complete** — all dependencies mapped, all consumers identified
2. **Decision documented** — ADR drafted with alternatives + trade-offs
3. **Contract locked** — interface signed, versioned, consumers notified
4. **Complexity within budget** — complexity audit verdict GREEN
5. **Non-functionals specified** — at least latency, throughput, error rate declared

**Recovery:** On checkpoint fail, revert to last-locked checkpoint, surface gap, AskUserQuestion: A) Re-loop from previous checkpoint with operator-provided context / B) Accept gap with concern (logs to ADR) / C) Raise help (escalate to operator).

**Continuation-after-fix:** Resume at the failed checkpoint, not from start. Job state preserves loop position.

**Raise help triggers:**

- New dependency tree-shake reveals a service the operator didn't know existed → raise help (operator confirms scope)
- ADR alternatives all score within 5% of each other → raise help (operator picks)
- Contract change breaks ≥3 consumers → raise help (operator decides migration path)

**Profile preferences (under `engineering.tech_architecture.*`):**

```yaml
engineering:
  tech_architecture:
    api_style: rest                      # rest | graphql | grpc | mixed
    versioning: semver-major-uri         # semver-major-uri | accept-header | none
    complexity_budget_cyclomatic: 12
    complexity_budget_cognitive: 18
    require_adr_on:
      - new_dependency
      - new_service
      - breaking_api_change
    architectural_review_required_above_loc: 500
```

## 3.4 Module spec — `data-architecture` (DA)

**Purpose:** When the work touches data models, schemas, storage, migrations, or analytics, invoke DA to produce schema-grade decisions and migrations.

**Granularities:**

| Entry | When | Outputs |
|---|---|---|
| `/li:da full` | new datastore / major migration | data-model.md + schema definitions + migration plan + retention policy + access patterns |
| `/li:da loop` | iterative schema refinement | revised schema + diff + backward-compat analysis |
| `/li:da single --action <name>` | targeted | one of: schema-design / migration-plan / index-audit / query-perf / data-flow / retention-policy / pii-scan |

**Sub-skills (proposed):**

- `da-schema-design` — entity-relationship modeling, normalization vs denormalization decisions
- `da-migration-plan` — zero-downtime migration sequencing
- `da-index-audit` — index coverage vs query pattern map
- `da-query-perf` — explain-plan analysis, N+1 detection, slow-query identification
- `da-data-flow` — provenance + transformation chain documentation
- `da-retention-policy` — per-entity TTL + deletion-cascade rules
- `da-pii-scan` — PII fingerprint detection (composes with security-compliance module)

**Agents (mostly existing):**

- `agents/engineering/DatabaseDesigner.md` (existing — primary)
- `agents/engineering/DataPipelineDesigner.md` (existing)
- `agents/engineering/SchemaMigrator.md` (NEW — distinct from generic Migrator)

**Hooks:**

- `schema-breaking-change-warn` (NEW) — pre-migration file save: warns if column removed/renamed without backward-compat shim
- `pii-in-schema-warn` (NEW) — pre-commit on schema file: pattern-match PII field names
- `retention-policy-required-warn` (NEW) — new entity without TTL declared

**Checkpoints:**

1. **Access patterns documented** — operator confirms top 5 query patterns
2. **Schema normalized** OR explicit denormalization with rationale
3. **Migration tested** in shadow environment
4. **Retention policy declared** per entity
5. **PII fields tagged** with classification

**Recovery / continuation / raise-help:** same pattern as TA.

**Profile preferences (under `engineering.data_architecture.*`):**

```yaml
engineering:
  data_architecture:
    primary_engine: postgres             # postgres | mysql | sqlite | cosmos | dynamodb | mixed
    naming: snake_case
    migration_tool: native               # native | flyway | liquibase | alembic | prisma
    require_explain_on_new_query: true
    pii_classification_required: true
    retention_default_days: 365
```

## 3.5 Module spec — `security-compliance` (SC)

**Purpose:** Uplift of existing security + compliance infrastructure into a cohesive module. Lintel today has 8 security agents + 6 compliance agents + 13 compliance skills + 7 block-hooks. They're not orchestrated.

**Granularities:**

| Entry | When | Outputs |
|---|---|---|
| `/li:sc full` | new feature, customer-bound | threat-model + secret-scan + dependency-audit + privacy-boundary + compliance-gate verdict |
| `/li:sc loop` | iterative tightening | revised threat-model + diff + remediation plan |
| `/li:sc single --action <name>` | targeted | one of: threat-model / secret-scan / sbom / oauth-review / dependency-audit / privacy-boundary / license-scan / agt-tier-check |

**Sub-skills:** Mostly existing — module orchestrates rather than creates. New: `sc-orchestrator` (the module's entry) and `sc-remediation-plan` (specs the gap-closing work).

**Agents:** All 8 security + 6 compliance agents, plus `SCOrchestrator` (NEW).

**Hooks:** All existing block-hooks. New: `compliance-gate-pre-merge` (pre-merge: runs the full SC verdict, blocks if RED).

**Checkpoints:**

1. **Threat model current** (drafted or updated ≤90 days)
2. **No CRITICAL/HIGH CVEs** in dependency audit
3. **No secrets in diff** (entropy + pattern scan PASS)
4. **Privacy boundaries respected** (PrivacyBoundaryAudit PASS)
5. **OAuth flows reviewed** if any authn touched
6. **License compliance verified** (SBOM PASS)
7. **AGT tier stamped** if agentic system

**Recovery / continuation / raise-help:** SC has the strictest raise-help — any CRITICAL finding raises immediately, not after retry-loop. Operator decides accept-with-attestation or remediate.

**Profile preferences (under `engineering.security_compliance.*`):**

```yaml
engineering:
  security_compliance:
    threat_model_refresh_days: 90
    cve_severity_block: high            # critical | high | medium
    require_sbom: true
    require_pii_classification: true
    oauth_review_on_authn_change: true
    agt_tier_required: when_agentic
    licensing_allowed: [mit, apache-2.0, bsd-2, bsd-3, mpl-2.0]
    licensing_blocked: [agpl, sspl]
```

## 3.6 Module spec — `devops-hosting` (DH)

**Purpose:** When the work needs deployment, infrastructure, CI/CD, observability, or runtime concerns, invoke DH. Lintel today has 7 devops agents + EV2/OneBranch validation + brand-staleness + some hooks — not orchestrated.

**Granularities:**

| Entry | When | Outputs |
|---|---|---|
| `/li:dh full` | new service / infra setup | infra-plan + ci-pipeline + observability-config + runbook + cost-model |
| `/li:dh loop` | iterative reliability tightening | revised SLO + diff + remediation plan |
| `/li:dh single --action <name>` | targeted | one of: ci-design / infra-as-code / observability-setup / runbook-draft / cost-audit / rollback-plan / canary-config |

**Sub-skills (proposed):**

- `dh-ci-design` — pipeline stages + gates + parallelism
- `dh-infra-as-code` — Terraform/Bicep/CDK module spec
- `dh-observability-setup` — metric + log + trace plan with SLI declaration
- `dh-runbook-draft` — operational playbook per failure mode
- `dh-cost-audit` — resource cost model + rightsizing recommendations
- `dh-rollback-plan` — per-change-class rollback procedure
- `dh-canary-config` — progressive rollout spec

**Agents (mostly existing):**

- `agents/devops/DevOpsToolchain.md` (existing — primary)
- `agents/devops/TerraformReviewer.md`
- `agents/devops/EV2PipelineAuditor.md`
- `agents/devops/K8sManifestReviewer.md`
- `agents/devops/GHActionsReviewer.md`
- `agents/devops/OneBranchReviewer.md`
- `agents/devops/PerformanceAnalyzer.md`
- `agents/devops/SREOrchestrator.md` (NEW — module entry)

**Hooks:**

- `infra-drift-warn` (NEW) — pre-deploy: warns if declared IaC diverges from actual cloud state
- `slo-uncovered-warn` (NEW) — new endpoint without SLI declared
- `cost-spike-warn` (NEW) — change estimated to >$X/mo without rationale

**Checkpoints:**

1. **CI pipeline declared** with gates
2. **IaC current** (terraform plan = no-drift)
3. **SLI/SLO specified** per new endpoint
4. **Runbook covers** known failure modes
5. **Rollback procedure** documented + tested
6. **Cost model** within budget

**Recovery / continuation / raise-help:** Same pattern.

**Profile preferences (under `engineering.devops_hosting.*`):**

```yaml
engineering:
  devops_hosting:
    primary_cloud: azure                 # azure | aws | gcp | hybrid | self-hosted
    ci_platform: github-actions          # github-actions | ev2 | onebranch | azure-pipelines | gitlab-ci
    iac_tool: bicep                      # bicep | terraform | cdk | pulumi
    observability_stack: app-insights    # app-insights | datadog | grafana-loki | otel
    slo_default_availability: 99.5
    cost_budget_alert_pct: 80
    canary_required_above_users: 10000
```

## 3.7 Module spec — `testing-qa` (TQ)

**Purpose:** When the work needs test strategy, coverage planning, regression protection, or QA validation, invoke TQ. Today: `tests/runner/` exists, behavior-pilot is the only behavior test, ~80 v3 skills have presence-tests only (gap 6.9).

**Granularities:**

| Entry | When | Outputs |
|---|---|---|
| `/li:tq full` | new feature requires test strategy | test-plan.md + coverage-target + harness-setup + regression-baseline + qa-checklist |
| `/li:tq loop` | iterative coverage tightening | revised plan + diff + new tests written + verdict |
| `/li:tq single --action <name>` | targeted | one of: coverage-audit / regression-test / mutation-test / e2e-design / contract-test / load-test / flakiness-hunt |

**Sub-skills (proposed):**

- `tq-coverage-audit` — line / branch / mutation coverage scoring
- `tq-regression-design` — diff-driven regression test selection
- `tq-mutation-test` — mutmut / Stryker-style mutation runs
- `tq-e2e-design` — end-to-end flow specs + acceptance criteria
- `tq-contract-test` — Pact-style consumer-producer contract verification
- `tq-load-test` — load model + acceptance thresholds
- `tq-flakiness-hunt` — flaky-test fingerprint + remediation

**Agents (existing + new):**

- `agents/engineering/TestRunner.md` (existing — primary)
- `agents/engineering/RegressionDetective.md` (existing)
- `agents/engineering/QAOrchestrator.md` (NEW — module entry)
- `agents/engineering/FlakinessHunter.md` (NEW)

**Hooks:**

- `coverage-drop-warn` (NEW) — pre-merge: coverage of changed lines below threshold
- `flaky-test-quarantine-warn` (NEW) — test fails intermittently → suggest quarantine
- `behavior-test-missing-warn` (NEW) — new skill without behavior test (closes gap 6.9 systemically)

**Checkpoints:**

1. **Coverage target met** per file class (unit ≥80, behavior ≥60, e2e key-path ≥1)
2. **Regression suite** covers diff-touched code paths
3. **No flaky tests** in critical path
4. **E2E acceptance** met for new user-flows
5. **Contract tests** PASS for changed interfaces

**Recovery / continuation / raise-help:** TQ raises help when coverage gap is structural (can't be reached without refactor).

**Profile preferences (under `engineering.testing_qa.*`):**

```yaml
engineering:
  testing_qa:
    unit_coverage_target: 80
    behavior_coverage_target: 60
    require_regression_on_diff: true
    mutation_test_on_critical: true
    e2e_required_for_user_flows: true
    flakiness_tolerance_pct: 0
    test_runner: pytest                  # pytest | vitest | jest | go-test | bun-test | …
```

## 3.8 Composition — full engineering pass

When operator invokes `/li:cycle --mode customer-engagement` with the active pack declaring engineering-domain coverage, the cycle's BUILD phase composes domains in order:

```
BUILD-phase composition (operator-configurable):
   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │   01 · tech-architecture (TA)                               │
   │        ↓ contract-locked checkpoint                          │
   │   02 · data-architecture (DA)                                │
   │        ↓ schema-locked checkpoint                            │
   │   03 · implementation (code emit per plan.md)                │
   │        ↓ atomic-commit per task                              │
   │   04 · security-compliance (SC)                              │
   │        ↓ no-CRITICAL-finding checkpoint                      │
   │   05 · devops-hosting (DH)                                   │
   │        ↓ pipeline-green checkpoint                           │
   │   06 · testing-qa (TQ)                                       │
   │        ↓ coverage-targets-met checkpoint                     │
   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                            ↓
                  REVIEW (cross-domain consistency)
                            ↓
                          SHIP
```

Each module's exit checkpoint feeds into the next module's input verification. A failure in any module triggers its own recovery loop without affecting downstream modules' state.

## 3.9 Single-action entry — "we are not the dumb tool"

Operator's stated value. Implemented via the `single` granularity on every module:

```
/li:ta single --action api-design          → just API design, returns spec
/li:sc single --action threat-model        → just threat model, returns model
/li:dh single --action ci-design           → just CI design, returns pipeline yaml
/li:tq single --action coverage-audit      → just coverage audit, returns report
```

These are SHORT (typically 5-15 min, ~3-10k tokens). Operator picks granularity. Lintel respects it.

## 3.10 Chapter 3 risks

- **Risk: 5 modules × ~7 sub-skills × 2-3 agents each = 100+ net-new artifacts.** Mitigation: ship one module at a time per Chapter 5 sequencing; reuse existing agents wherever possible; each module-PR includes a "what's net-new vs reused" inventory.
- **Risk: full engineering pass is slow.** Mitigation: each module can run in parallel where dependencies don't bind (TA + DA can interleave; SC + DH can parallelize after implementation; TQ is final). Document parallel-eligible boundaries explicitly.
- **Risk: operator preferences explode in complexity.** Mitigation: each module ships with a "default preferences" file that's good enough for 80% of cases. Operator only customizes the 20% that matter for their work.

# CHAPTER 4 — Infrastructure-for-infrastructure discipline

> This chapter is my interpretation of the operator's meta-process note. Honoring the request by giving it as much architectural weight as the others.

## 4.1 What the operator asked for

Verbatim from the message: *"Tycker även vi ska bygga ut vår process kring det som är resulterande infrastruktur av något om något är att bygga infrastruktur dvs hehe."*

Parsed: when the WORK is "build infrastructure for Lintel itself" (like v3.8 jobs, this v4.0 reframe, future skill-family additions), the process should be different from feature work. The output is structure, not content. The risks are different. The validation is different.

My interpretation: introduce a **meta-infra mode** + a discipline that distinguishes "harness work" from "feature work" and applies the right gates.

## 4.2 The `meta-infra` mode envelope

A sixth mode joins the five existing envelopes (hotfix / customer-engagement / research-dive / demo-prep / internal-tool):

```yaml
meta-infra:
  phases: ALL_8 (heavier REVIEW, heavier CAPTURE)
  cap: 600k soft / 900k hard
  audience: operator + future-operator
  voice_tier: internal
  compliance: scaffolding-only (skip customer-facing gates)
  cost_estimate: ~50-100k tokens, 2-5 hours
  use_when: change touches skills/ · agents/ · hooks/ · bin/_*.sh · install/ · LAYERS.md · core templates
```

**Activates when:**

- Cycle target files match `^(skills|agents|hooks|bin)/.*` patterns
- OR operator explicitly invokes `/li:cycle --mode meta-infra`
- OR a previous-cycle CAPTURE flagged the change as "structural"

SENSE detects via cwd + diff signature and recommends meta-infra mode auto.

## 4.3 Meta-infra-specific gates

Beyond the standard cycle gates, meta-infra mode adds four mandatory gates inside REVIEW:

### Gate M1 — Structure-impact analysis

Before any structural change merges, declare:

```
Affected: skills/X/ + hooks/Y/
Pattern delta: <what changes in the SHAPE, not just the content>
Backward-compat: <which existing usages continue to work as-is>
Migration path: <if break-changes, the migration discipline>
Forward-compat: <what future patterns this enables or forecloses>
```

Stored as `docs/v4.x/structure-changes/<date>-<slug>.md`. CAPTURE auto-creates from cycle context.

### Gate M2 — Compatibility audit

Mechanical: run a sweep over all 141 skills + 18 hooks + 83 agents asking:

- Does this change affect frontmatter contracts they depend on?
- Does this change rename or move a referenced path?
- Does this change new-default a previously-optional field?
- Does this change a shared helper (`bin/_aliases.sh`, `bin/_jobs.sh`)?

Output: `compatibility-audit.md` listing every affected artifact + risk class. Empty audit = green. Non-empty audit = review per item.

### Gate M3 — Regression shape-tests

Distinct from regression behavior tests. Shape-tests verify:

- frontmatter-lint still passes for ALL skills (not just changed ones)
- agents-categorized.sh still passes
- catalog regenerates without diff
- existing v1_alias / deprecated_aliases declarations still resolve

When a shape-test fails, the cycle BLOCKS at REVIEW. No bypass without explicit override + audit.

### Gate M4 — Future-operator validation

Operator + Claude walk a fresh-cold-session scenario:

- "Six months from now, an operator (could be you) opens this for the first time. Read only the README + LAYERS.md + the affected concept doc. Can they understand what changed and why?"

If no → CAPTURE must produce a concept doc + a migration note. If yes → proceed.

## 4.4 Output contract: change-log + migration-guide as one document

Standard cycle CAPTURE produces lessons.md + ADR + memory.md updates. Meta-infra CAPTURE produces all of those PLUS a `MIGRATION.md` entry under `docs/v4.x/migrations/`:

```markdown
# Migration: <date> — <change summary>

## What changed (shape)
<the structural delta from Gate M1>

## What still works without action
<list of unchanged callsites>

## What requires migration
<callsite> → <new-shape> (estimated effort: <S/M/L>)

## Compatibility window
- Grace period: <until-when>
- Removal date: <when the old shape is removed>
- Tracker: tasks/memory.md entry <name>

## Test discipline
- Shape-tests added: <which>
- Regression coverage: <statement>

## Rollback procedure
<if this migration goes wrong, here's how>
```

These migration notes become operator-discoverable via a new `/li:migrations` skill that surfaces pending migrations at SENSE if the active worktree has callsites still on the old shape.

## 4.5 The `/li:migrations` skill (NEW)

Sister to `/li:status`. Surfaces:

- Active migration windows (changes shipped, grace period ongoing)
- Operator-callsites still on old shape
- Days remaining until removal
- Suggested action per callsite

Read-only. Doesn't migrate code automatically. Surfaces the work; operator decides.

## 4.6 When meta-infra applies vs not — the discipline

| Work type | Mode | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Build a new feature in a customer engagement | customer-engagement | content work, not infrastructure |
| Fix a bug in an existing skill | hotfix | targeted fix, no structural change |
| Add a new skill to an existing family | internal-tool | additive, no contract change |
| Add a new agent category (like v3.7 frontend/) | **meta-infra** | new structural pattern, must validate |
| Change frontmatter contract | **meta-infra** | affects every skill/agent |
| Move a bin/ helper | **meta-infra** | affects every caller |
| Rename a skill (per alias-mekanism) | **meta-infra** | affects callsites + plugin manifests |
| Add a new mode envelope | **meta-infra** | affects cycle behavior |
| Add a new layer to LAYERS.md | **meta-infra** | foundational change |

When in doubt, SENSE recommends meta-infra. Operator can downgrade after the impact analysis (Gate M1) if it confirms a smaller surface than first detected.

## 4.7 Chapter 4 risks

- **Risk: meta-infra mode adds overhead that disincentivizes structural improvements.** Mitigation: the gates are mostly mechanical (M2 + M3 run automatically); only M1 + M4 require thinking. Net additional time ~30 min for typical structural change. Worth the regression-protection trade.
- **Risk: operator skips meta-infra to ship faster.** Mitigation: SENSE auto-recommends; operator can override with `--mode internal-tool` but the override is audit-logged. After 3 audited overrides, SENSE surfaces a "your recent structural changes have skipped meta-infra — review?" prompt.
- **Risk: migration notes become bureaucratic theater.** Mitigation: `MIGRATION.md` is short-by-design (5 sections, ~20 lines typical). Operator can `/li:migrations dismiss <id>` if a migration becomes irrelevant.

## 4.8 Meta-application: this v4.0 reframe IS a meta-infra cycle

The reframe itself is harness-on-harness work. We should dogfood meta-infra mode immediately:

- Gate M1 (structure-impact): this doc IS the impact analysis
- Gate M2 (compatibility-audit): pack-resolver test harness (FR-A.7) + cross-skill `grep -r` sweep
- Gate M3 (regression shape-tests): existing test suite extended with frontmatter-contract tests
- Gate M4 (future-operator validation): operator review of this doc IS the validation

Closing the loop: shipping v4.0 IS the first meta-infra cycle execution.

# CHAPTER 5 — How these compose · ship sequencing · risk

## 5.1 Cross-chapter dependency graph

```
Chapter 4 (meta-infra mode)
       ↓ governs how all subsequent ship
Chapter 1.A (spine extraction)
       ↓
Chapter 1.B (pack architecture) — adds brief_forge: block to pack.yaml
       ↓                          ↑
Chapter 1.D (CAIP-SE lift)        Chapter 2.B (envelope schema — small, can ship anytime)
       ↓                          ↑
Chapter 1.C (navigation)          Chapter 2.A (Brief Forge — depends on envelope + pack)
       ↓                          ↑
                                  Chapter 2.C (wiki gen — depends on all above)
       ↓                          ↑
       └──→ ENGINEERING DEPTH (Chapter 3) ←──┘
            One domain at a time, rollout in any order
```

## 5.2 Ship phases

**Phase 1 — v4.0-alpha (~5-7 CC-days):** meta-infra mode + spine extraction
- Ship the meta-infra mode FIRST. We need it to govern Chapter 1.A which IS structural.
- Then ship Chapter 1.A (spine extraction) under meta-infra discipline. This is the proof-of-process.
- Output: spine works pack-neutral; meta-infra mode active.

**Phase 2 — v4.0-beta (~5-7 CC-days):** pack architecture + CAIP-SE lift + envelope schema
- Chapter 1.B (pack architecture) under meta-infra.
- Chapter 1.D (CAIP-SE pack) under standard internal-tool (it's content-migration).
- Chapter 2.B (envelope schema) under meta-infra (small but structural).
- Output: packs work; operator's daily workflow continues via caip-se pack; envelope schema exists for future Brief Forge plumbing.

**Phase 3 — v4.0-rc (~5-7 CC-days):** navigation + Brief Forge + wiki gen
- Chapter 1.C (navigation) under meta-infra.
- Chapter 2.A (Brief Forge) under meta-infra (large structural addition).
- Chapter 2.C (wiki gen) under standard internal-tool (it reads existing sources, doesn't change them).
- Output: every workflow_root has navigation; every hand-off goes through Brief Forge; wiki is generated.

**Phase 4 — v4.0 ship + v4.1 engineering depth (~2-3 CC-days per module, 5 modules = 10-15 days)**
- v4.0 ships at end of Phase 3.
- Chapter 3 modules ship one at a time as v4.1 / v4.2 / v4.3 / v4.4 / v4.5 — operator picks order based on engagement needs.
- Each module ships under standard internal-tool (they're additive feature work, not structural).

**Total estimate: 17-27 CC-days for v4.0 ship + ~10-15 CC-days for full engineering-depth rollout = ~30-40 CC-days for complete v4.x.**

## 5.3 What can ship NOW vs needs decisions

| Item | Ready? | If not, why |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 1 (meta-infra + spine) | YES | All decisions locked |
| Phase 2 (packs + CAIP-SE + envelope) | YES | All decisions locked |
| Phase 3 (navigation + Brief Forge + wiki) | YES | All decisions locked |
| Phase 4 each module | DECISIONS NEEDED | Per-module: operator confirms preferences scope + sub-skill enumeration |

## 5.4 Cross-cutting risks

- **Risk: scope creep across 5 chapters.** Mitigation: each phase is independently shippable; if Phase 3 reveals Chapter 2 needs to change, we have a clean point to pause and revise.
- **Risk: pack-policy explosion.** Mitigation: enforce that pack.yaml stays minimal; complex pack-policy lives in pack's own files (`brand/`, `compliance/`, etc.) not in pack.yaml.
- **Risk: navigation orientator is wrong on first runs.** Mitigation: auto-mode level (b); risk_level defaults conservative; LLM-escalation budget keeps cost bounded.
- **Risk: Brief Forge fails open (lets bad payloads through).** Mitigation: evaluators must be deterministic enough to fail closed by default. Override requires explicit `--no-brief-forge` flag + audit.
- **Risk: wiki gen becomes stale because nobody runs it.** Mitigation: pre-commit hook on structural changes; CI check.
- **Risk: engineering-domain modules duplicate work that already exists.** Mitigation: each module starts with `grep`-driven inventory of existing skills/agents; module is orchestration layer + new gates only.

## Operator validation criteria (when v4.0 ships fully)

The system passes when all of these are true:

1. **Pack neutrality:** `grep -r "Trailblazer\|CAIP-SE\|RAIS\|OneCS" skills/ agents/ hooks/` returns no execution-path matches.
2. **Pack swap:** `/li:pack-switch caip-se` produces today's behavior. `/li:pack-switch _default` produces neutral behavior. No code changes.
3. **Navigation guarantee:** A `workflow_root: true` skill without `navigation:` block is rejected at load. The architectural guarantee holds.
4. **Brief Forge coverage:** Every hand-off in cycle/plan/build/ship/capture runs through Brief Forge. Override-with-audit works. <1s overhead on default-pack hand-offs measured.
5. **Envelope adoption:** Every hand-off produces an envelope. `/li:envelope-replay <id> --dry-run` works end-to-end.
6. **Wiki accuracy:** `bin/li-wiki-gen` produces a wiki that matches current 141 skills × 83 agents × 18 hooks × N packs. Idempotent (re-run = no diff).
7. **Engineering depth:** Each of the 5 modules can be invoked standalone (`/li:ta single --action api-design` etc.) and complete its loop with checkpoint verdict.
8. **Meta-infra discipline:** Any change to `skills/` / `agents/` / `hooks/` / `bin/` defaults to meta-infra mode. Gate M2 (compatibility audit) runs automatically.
9. **Migration discipline:** `MIGRATION.md` entries exist for every structural change shipped under meta-infra. `/li:migrations` surfaces pending migrations at SENSE.
10. **Operator validation:** Six months after v4.0 ships, an MS colleague (not in CAIP-SE) clones the repo, runs `/li:pack-new`, builds their own pack in 10 min, uses Lintel without touching CAIP-SE content. Indie builder does the same with `_default`. Operator's daily workflow unchanged.

---

## What I'm flagging as risk to operator

Five concerns I want surfaced before code starts:

**R1 — The v4.0 reframe is a fundamental contract change.** Anyone using Lintel for CAIP-SE work today must switch to the caip-se pack post-FR-D. The switch should be automated (install script detects existing usage, switches default), but operators relying on aliases or scripts that hardcode paths will break. **Mitigation:** Phase 2 ships with a `/li:v4-migrate` skill that walks operator through the swap.

**R2 — Brief Forge latency claim (<1s) needs telemetry from day one.** If it's not measurable, the claim is unfalsifiable. **Mitigation:** envelope's TAIL records `brief_forge_results.duration_ms` per evaluator. Ship a `/li:forge-stats` skill in v4.0-rc that surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency per evaluator type.

**R3 — Engineering-domain modules risk over-specification.** Each module's spec above is ambitious. Real-world friction may force scope reduction. **Mitigation:** ship each module's `full` granularity LAST (after `single` + `loop` are proven). Operator picks which `single` actions ship first per module.

**R4 — Meta-infra mode adds friction; operator may resent it.** Especially on small refactors that touch a skill file. **Mitigation:** SENSE auto-detection is generous (only triggers on patterns that obviously affect contracts). Small additive changes (new skill in existing family) stay in internal-tool mode. The threshold is "does this change the SHAPE that other code depends on?"

**R5 — Wiki generation may obscure handcrafted documentation.** Some docs (LAYERS.md, CORE-PRINCIPLES.md) should NEVER be auto-generated. **Mitigation:** Wiki generator has an explicit `IGNORE_PATHS:` list; LAYERS, CORE-PRINCIPLES, lessons.md, memory.md, ADRs are NEVER overwritten. Wiki includes them by `<include path>` not by replacement.

---

## What this doc does NOT specify

Out of scope for v4.0; reserved for later or operator-discretion:

- **Pack marketplace.** Operator's spec mentioned `/li:pack-export` for sharing. v4.0 ships the mechanic; no public marketplace until ecosystem proves out.
- **Multi-pack stacking.** Can a session have TWO packs active? Operator's spec implies one at a time. v4.0 enforces one-at-a-time; multi-pack deferred to v5.0.
- **Per-skill brief_forge_handoffs schema details.** Operator's spec mentions skills must declare. v4.0 enforces existence; the specific schema is defined within the FR-A PR (not pre-committed here).
- **Engineering modules beyond the 5.** "Documentation" / "Performance" / "Observability" could each become modules. v4.0 ships these five; future expansion follows the same pattern.
- **CI integration for shape-tests.** v4.0 ships shape-tests as test-suite additions; integrating into matrix-CI (test on multiple Python versions, etc.) is post-v4.0.

## Closing thought — why this matters

Operator said in the message: *"This is maybe a flexibility of the system as whole that I want to be replicated across all areas of this action-system, across all workflows, i want this system to be flexible, comprehensive, capable, iterable, modular and opinionated etc from the start."*

v4.0 is exactly that: every chapter shipped together produces a system that is:

- **Flexible** — packs make identity swappable; navigation makes entry/exit operator-chosen
- **Comprehensive** — engineering domains cover the depth; modules compose to full coverage
- **Capable** — Brief Forge gates hand-offs; envelopes preserve provenance; wiki documents truth
- **Iterable** — every module has loops with checkpoints; meta-infra mode protects iteration of the iteration-machine itself
- **Modular** — packs are modular; modules are modular; sub-skills within modules are modular
- **Opinionated** — defaults are sharp; recommendations are explicit; novice-protection is refused

This is not a refactor. It's the architecture v3.x has been pointing toward, finally consolidated. Ship sequence preserves operator daily workflow throughout. Meta-infra mode protects against the refactor-of-the-refactor regression that this scope of work usually invites.

Operator's call on whether to greenlight Phase 1 immediately or iterate this doc first.

## Appendix C — operator stance carried through, verbatim

Operator told me to honor intent. The stances carried through every chapter:

- **Bold + effective + operator carries responsibility.** Every gate ships with override + audit. No paternalism.
- **Refusal of padding for novice protection.** No hand-holding. Pack interview asks essentials in condensed form.
- **Opinionated about what spine demands from any workflow.** Navigation and brief_forge_handoffs are mandatory, not optional.
- **Sequential where it pays, parallel where it helps.** Engineering modules compose sequentially by default but declare parallel-eligible boundaries.
- **Mechanical first, LLM on escalation.** Brief Forge evaluators, orientator routing, all default to mechanical parsing with budgeted LLM fallback.
- **Defense through transparency, not blocking.** Override-with-audit is the pattern. Trust the operator.
- **Compounding edge through discipline, not toolchain.** Pack vault, envelope log, generated wiki — all compound over time.

## The 7 P1 findings (must resolve before code)

### S0-P1.1 — v4.0 is contradictorily defined (Chapter 3 is both in and out)
- Ship plan (lines 824–847) puts Chapter 3 in v4.1-4.5.
- Operator validation criterion #7 (line 917) requires Chapter 3 modules invokable at v4.0 ship.
- Pick one: (a) pull Ch.3 out of v4.0 entirely, OR (b) reduce criterion #7 to "pattern shipped + 1 reference module proves it."
- **Recommend (b)** — ship the engineering-module PATTERN in v4.0 + TA module as reference; defer other 4 modules to v4.1+.

### S0-P1.2 — The puddle path is hidden
- Doc says "Lintel already does most of this informally" (line 82) but never offers a minimum-viable v4.0.
- **Add v4.0-minimal variant**: Ch.1 + Ch.2 + Ch.4 (no Ch.3). ~17-20 CC-days. ~12-15 net-new skills. Lets operator pick lake-or-puddle explicitly.

### S0-P1.3 — Chapter 3 breaks L-001 (scaffolding-not-content)
- 5 modules × 7 sub-skills = 35 net-new skills that ARE the content (`ta-api-design`, `da-pii-scan`, `dh-runbook-draft` etc.)
- L-001 says ship the pattern + ONE canonical example.
- **Fix:** Ship 1 reference module (TA, per C3-D1 default) + `<module>-template` skill family. Defer 4 modules × 7 sub-skills = 28 skills. **Drops scope ~30%.**

### 1-P1.1 — Pack-resolver is critical-path singleton with no failure-mode spec
- Used by 30+ skills. What happens on malformed pack.yaml? Resolver bug? Mid-cycle staleness?
- **Add §1.2.1** "Pack-resolver failure semantics": parse-error → hard-fail SENSE; bug → fall-back-to-_default + warn; in-session value cached at SENSE, immutable for cycle lifetime.

### 1-P1.2 — Engineering domain modules overlap existing families (L-002 violation)
- Verified overlaps: `tq-coverage-audit` ↔ `generate-qa`. `sc-orchestrator` ↔ `compliance-gate`. `dh-ci-design` ↔ Azure-toolbox. `ta-api-design` ↔ `APIDesigner` agent.
- SC module says "orchestrates rather than creates" (line 437) — TA/DA/DH/TQ should follow same discipline.
- **Fix:** Per-module mandatory L-002 inventory before sub-skill list. Where overlaps exist, module REUSES, doesn't recreate.

### 3-P1.1 — Validation criterion #10 is unmechanical
- "Six months after v4.0 ships, MS colleague clones the repo..." cannot be tested at ship-time.
- **Fix:** Replace with `/li:pack-new --interactive --dry-run` produces valid pack.yaml in ≤10 prompts. Move colleague-validation to a post-ship hypothesis-tracker.

### 3-P1.2 — "Shape-tests" referenced 5× but never enumerated
- Gate M3 cannot fire until shape-tests exist.
- **Fix:** §4.3.1 — Initial 4 shape-tests: `frontmatter-lint-all`, `agents-categorized`, `catalog-regenerates-clean`, `deprecated-aliases-resolve`. Each is its own file under `tests/shape/`. Documented in `tests/shape/_README.md`.

### 4-P1.1 — Engineering "full pass" composition exceeds customer-engagement 500k cap
- 5 modules × ~80k tokens each = 400k of 500k cap. Leaves 100k for OTHER 7 cycle phases. Math doesn't work.
- **Fix:** Either (a) per-module sub-budget allocation, OR (b) raise customer-engagement cap to 750k for full-pass mode, OR (c) introduce `customer-engagement-deep` as 6th mode envelope.

## The most surgical P2s

- **2-P2.4 — 14 "open decisions" are 14 recommendations dressed as questions.** Only C3-D1 (which module ships first) is genuinely undecided. **Fix:** Rename section "Defaults pending operator sign-off." Add separate §"Real open decisions" with only the genuine forks.
- **2-P2.1 — Module YAML pattern repeated 5× with subtle drift.** TQ section omits recovery/continuation/raise-help spec that TA gets in full (line 577 is 1 line vs TA's 10). **Fix:** Factor pattern into §3.2 template; each module lists ONLY pack-specific deltas.
- **2-P2.2 — Frontmatter field has 3 names** (`brief_forge:`, `brief_forge_handoffs:`, no canonical anywhere). **Fix:** Pick `brief_forge_handoffs:`. Search-replace.
- **2-P1.1 — Three different docs path conventions** (`docs/v4.0/`, `docs/v4.x/`, mixed). **Fix:** Pick `docs/v4.x/<artifact-class>/<date>-<slug>.md` for all meta-infra outputs.
- **1-P2.1 — Brief Forge fires on every operator→skill invocation.** Cumulative-per-day overhead unaccounted. **Fix:** Add cold-path bypass: trivial skills (read-only, no spawn) declare `brief_forge_handoffs: skip` in frontmatter.
